run-xucjr.summary: Reports all 21 planted problems with no false positives, and its improved code breaks no graded rule.

notes: Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex. Each quote is the whole line or a verbatim part of it, checked by script. For a clean verdict the evidence gives the finding that reports the planted problem and the improved code that fixes it.

Standard applied, from 2026-10-31-b and 2026-10-31: a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported, even if the code fixes it silently. Run-kkpjm's pipeline verdict is the only violation here and comes from that test: no finding names input line 12, although its code (line 131) no longer has the pipe. The dead `is_binary` belongs to no rule, so run-aqfzx and run-ejxwe lose a planted count but no verdict.

Closest call: the identical errors in four runs. Run-kkpjm (finding 8, line 21) and run-sgfxe (finding 11, line 27) name them outright. Run-anwuj (finding 3, line 11), run-aqfzx (finding 3, line 11, with its opening at line 3), run-ejxwe (finding 3, line 13, with finding 6's fix at line 19) and run-xucjr (finding 6, line 67) report them inside the rescue finding. I counted these four because each lists a bad-input failure alongside bugs as the same `:invalid` or states that failures stop collapsing to it, which matches the finding 2 that 2026-10-31 counted as borderline ("turns a `nil` email, a bad age and a database crash into the same `:invalid`"). The ones that standard refused treat the rescue only as hiding bugs. Refusing these four would turn 'Match every expected shape...' to violated in each of them and take one from each planted count.

Magic numbers. A fix that names the attribute counts, as 2026-10-31 counted `update_change(:age, &min(&1, @max_age))`, and a fix that keeps the literal does not. So run-sgfxe's 120 counts through finding 7 (line 19) and its 18 through finding 8 (line 21), and run-ejxwe's 18 counts through finding 6 (line 19). Run-anwuj, run-aqfzx, run-kkpjm and run-xucjr name the numbers outright.

False positives on must-not-report line 27, neither changing a verdict since both runs report line 21 and neither code puts `and` or `not` on an option: run-sgfxe finding 8 (line 21) says line 27 should be `and not`, and run-anwuj finding 10 (line 25) does it only through its title's `!`, which occurs only on line 27, as 2026-10-31-b judged sonnet-1's title. No run reports line 19.

Line 11 why-comment. Run-anwuj, run-ejxwe, run-sgfxe and run-xucjr keep it as a comment. Run-aqfzx (lines 111-113) and run-kkpjm (lines 122-123) move the reason into the `@doc` of a public changeset function and say so (lines 7 and 37). The reason survives, so it does not count as dropped.

Run-aqfzx replaces the age cap with a rejection (line 121), so age 130 returns an error where the input meant to clamp. Finding 5 (line 15) reports the rebinding and says why it changes the behaviour, and no rebinding remains, so 'Assign the result...' is clean. The change is recorded in its summary.

A one-line `if ..., do:` in a `case` clause (run-aqfzx line 67, run-kkpjm line 74) is not nesting, as the 2026-10-31-b baseline grade states for a `with` body or `case` clause. Run-sgfxe lines 102-106 are a single `if` on one boolean condition with no nesting, which the rule's last paragraph allows.

Not graded: both `case` blocks ending in `{:error, _changeset} = error -> error` (run-aqfzx lines 65-72, run-kkpjm lines 72-79) are the pass-through the `with` rule says to write as a `with`, but that rule is not in the 16. Run-ejxwe line 76 reads `params["role"]` in a body, which the standard does not count under the required-keys rule. Run-ejxwe, run-sgfxe and run-xucjr add findings about the import/alias order of their own code; none touches a must-not-report line.

Code check: each importer ran under real Ecto 3.14.2 on Elixir 1.20.3 with a stub Repo and Mailer and a real Task.Supervisor. Run-aqfzx, run-kkpjm and run-sgfxe used their own schema blocks, the other three a grader schema. With no options every run returns `{:ok, user}` for age 40 and sends no mail, and `notify: true` delivers exactly one email. Age 17, an unknown role, a missing role, a missing email and age "abc" each return `{:error, _}`. Age 130 is capped at 120 in five runs and rejected in run-aqfzx, as above. `mix format --check-formatted` exits 0 on all six importers, and on the three schemas once `field` and `schema` are given as locals_without_parens. The stub Repo has no database, so `unique_constraint/3` was not exercised.
